findingDetails.title: The Bottom Line calls 303 raw findings and partitions them into 121 kept plus a 332-row remainder, which cannot close
findingDetails.scopeProof: research.md:34 states the partition; research.md:632 gives 121 kept and 332 log rows; research.md:735 labels 303 as the merged registry key findings; the four state logs give 55 + 50 + 65 + 101 = 271 iteration-typed findings once pi-2 duplicate iteration 7 is removed
findingDetails.case: A reader checks the Bottom Line arithmetic. 121 rows survive and the regrade log holds 332 rows for the rest, so the raw total should be 453, not 303. A reader who trusts 303 concludes the log double-counts; a reader who trusts the log concludes the Bottom Line undercounts. Neither can tell which figure the rest of the document uses, and section 13 uses 303 for a third thing again.
findingDetails.claim: research.md:34 calls 303 raw findings and partitions them into 121 kept plus a remainder the regrade log covers with 332 rows, which cannot close; research.md:735 identifies 303 as the merged registry key-findings count, a different quantity from the raw findings the four lineages reported.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Looked for a sentence that reconciles 303 with 121 + 332. Section 8 note explains that a log row can group several origins, which makes log rows fewer than findings, not more, so it widens the gap. Checked whether 303 could be the raw count: the four state logs sum to 275 iteration-typed findingsCount values, 271 once pi-2 repeated iteration 7 is deduped. Checked whether 303 is a typo for 453: section 13 uses 303 independently as the merged registry key-findings count.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The sentence may intend 303 as the merged registry key findings and 121 as the rows that survived from that merged set, with the 332 log rows covering lineage findings that never entered the merged set. That reading is available, but the sentence says raw findings and for the rest, which is the partition reading, and it never names the merged registry.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to no finding if the sentence is reworded to name the merged registry key-findings count and to stop presenting 121 and 332 as a partition of it.

results.notes: The document own stated rules were checked against its content: the licence rule at research.md:26 against all 20 lift rows, D3 against the working tree, D4 against the phase and net-new placement of every row, D5 against section 7 citation rule, and the Bottom Line counts against sections 8 and 13. One gap, recorded as V2-R10-P2-001.
The packet has no checklist.md at Level 1, so there is no checklist to trace against.

011 five GPL rows break the licence rule -- ruled out: the section opening names the licence with two SOURCE tags and states every row below is mirror-only.
008 lift row 1 breaks the licence rule -- ruled out: the section opening carries the Apache-2.0 line and the NOTICE line.
303 is a typo for 453 -- ruled out: section 13 uses 303 independently as the merged registry key-findings count.
The regrade log double-counts -- ruled out: section 8 note explains that a log row can group several origins, and the 43 downgraded and 38 corrected rows are also kept rows.
Section 7 repeats findings instead of citing them -- ruled out: its opening states the citation rule and its entries carry S1/S2/S3 line citations with a New here note each.

Section 13 303 key findings is a second finding -- ruled out: it is the same defect seen from the other end, recorded once as V2-R10-P2-001.
